title: Coherent finite scalar restriction for sheafified and derived open extension
statement:
For finite commutative rings $A,B,C$ and homomorphisms $\varphi:A\to B$, $\psi:B\to C$, put $\chi=\psi\varphi$. For each scheme $T$ use constant ring sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $r_{\varphi,T}$ for restriction of module-sheaf scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and for its exact termwise functor on the unbounded derived categories. Write $\rho_T:r_{\varphi,T}r_{\psi,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\chi,T}$ for the canonical identification: on underlying abelian sheaves it is the identity and the two actions are $a m=\psi_T(\varphi_T(a))m$; on derived categories it is its termwise localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $R=A,B,C$, let $J_R=j_!^R$ be sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], which is exact [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]; $J_R$ also denotes its termwise localization. There is a natural isomorphism of module-sheaf functors
$$e_\varphi:J_A r_{\varphi,U}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\varphi,Z}J_B,$$
uniquely characterized by inducing the identity on the defining extension-by-zero presheaves before sheafification. It induces a natural isomorphism with the same endpoints on all of $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. For every $C$-module sheaf, every complex thereof and every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$, respectively, these specified comparisons satisfy
$$e_{\chi,K}\circ J_A(\rho_{U,K})=\rho_{Z,J_CK}\circ r_{\varphi,Z}(e_{\psi,K})\circ e_{\varphi,r_{\psi,U}K}.$$
For an identity coefficient map the comparison is the identity under the canonical identifications. No quasi-compactness of $j$, flatness of coefficient maps, boundedness or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For fixed-scalar sheaves, the published comparison is leftAdjointUniq for the composite adjunctions formed from open extension and restriction/coextension of scalars. Its unit equation, evaluated on a section and then at 1 in the coextended module, gives the open-unit normalization. Applying the open adjunction mate equivalence therefore sends this comparison to the identity restriction square.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03CY, extension-by-zero adjunction and section-normalized realization; adjunction mate argument in the Lean proof.

proof.text: The published realization comparison preserves each section. Consequently its comparison for a composite coefficient map is the composite of the two comparisons followed by the specified intrinsic scalar compositor. The inverse realization comparison is its adjunction mate, so the same composition law holds for the inverse realization comparisons. Paste the fixed open square with these two realization squares. Compatibility of mates with pasting identifies its mate with the inverse of sfOpenRestrictionCoefficientSquare. The mate unit equation proves the asserted normalization. Injectivity of the open adjunction hom equivalence, followed by cancellation of the coefficient-square component, proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03CY, extension-by-zero adjunction and section-normalized realization; adjunction mate argument in the Lean proof.

proof.text: The fixed-scalar comparison satisfies composition by the unit normalization and injectivity of the open-adjunction hom equivalence. Transport this equation through the realization comparisons. Their composition equations and naturality give the sheaf cocycle with both prescribed intrinsic scalar compositors. The canonical identity restriction comparison preserves every section; the identity specialization of the cocycle and naturality then give the sheaf identity law.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03CY, extension-by-zero adjunction and section-normalized realization; adjunction mate argument in the Lean proof.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf equations in every degree and use extensionality of complex morphisms. The comparison transformations and their inverses already give chain maps by naturality, so this proves the equations for all unbounded cochain complexes.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact termwise functors on unbounded complexes.

proof.text: Invert the scalar compositors in the sheaf cocycle by cancellation. Apply the existing general composition theorem for exact derived squares to the open-extension squares and these compositors, take its component at K, and cancel the invertible derived compositors. This is the required derived cocycle. Apply the existing exact-derived identity-square theorem to the inverse open comparison and the canonical identity restriction comparisons to obtain the derived identity equation.
